title: Composition of compact-support transport along powers of geometric Frobenius
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $p$ prime, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k$ its fixed algebraic closure. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ contained in the fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and write $a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Use the finite-coefficient categories and the functor $H(M)=R\Gamma_c(X,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}M)$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$, $g=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, as in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Write $P_r=L(g^r)^*$ and $Q_r=L(h^r)^*$, with derived pullback as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Fix one compactification $c_0=(X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X_0\xrightarrow{p_0}\operatorname{Spec}k_0)$ of $a_{X_0}$ in the sense of [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and use its base change $c$ to represent $Ra_{X!}$ (with the specified comparison maps if the fixed functor uses another representative). Use this same $c_0$ for every power below.

For each integer $r\geq1$ and $M\in D^b_c(X,A)$ define the direct transport along $g^r$ by
$$
\tau^{(r)}_{c,M}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(e_r(M))\circ\iota^{(r)}_{Ra_{X!}M}:H(M)\longrightarrow H(P_rM).
$$
Here $\iota^{(r)}_N:\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)\to\operatorname{Fib}_s(Q_rN)$ is the restriction--colimit-insertion--derived-pullback map of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] with $h$ replaced by $h^r$. The map $e_r:Q_rRa_{X!}\to Ra_{X!}P_r$ is the compactification exchange of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], formed with the fixed compactification $c_0$ over $k_0$ and with each induced geometric Frobenius automorphism replaced by its $r$-th power. Thus $\tau^{(1)}_{c,M}=\tau_{c,M}$ of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. For $m\geq1$ let $c_{m,M}:P_1P_mM\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{m+1}M$ be the inverse of the canonical pullback-composition identification of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] (for the constant coefficient ring sheaves A and the composable scheme maps g and g^m). Then for every $M\in D^b_c(X,A)$ and every integer $m\geq1$,
$$
\tau^{(m+1)}_{c,M}=H(c_{m,M})\circ\tau^{(1)}_{c,P_mM}\circ\tau^{(m)}_{c,M}.
$$
No Weil structure on $M$ is assumed.

proof.text: Work first with the specified representative $F=Rp_*j_!$ of $Ra_{X!}$ and put $J=j_!$, $R=Rp_*$, $B_r=L(\bar g^r)^*$, where $\bar g=\operatorname{id}_{\overline X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$. The degree-one squares for $p$ and $j$ commute and are Cartesian by [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian], applied to $p_0$ and $j_0$. Their power squares also commute: from $p\bar g=hp$ and $j g=\bar g j$ obtain $p\bar g^r=h^rp$ and $j g^r=\bar g^rj$ by induction. All horizontal maps are isomorphisms, since their inverses are the corresponding powers of the inverses. Such a commuting square is Cartesian: for maps $x:T\to\overline X$ and $y:T\to s$ with $p x=h^r y$, its unique lift is $\bar g^{-r}x$, since $p\bar g^{-r}x=h^{-r}px=y$; for the open square, given $x:T\to X$ and $y:T\to\overline X$ with $jx=\bar g^ry$, its unique lift is $g^{-r}x$, since $jg^{-r}x=\bar g^{-r}jx=y$. Thus the power squares have precisely the identifications used in the item. By [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], each $P_r$ preserves $D^b_c(X,A)$, so in particular $\tau^{(1)}_{c,P_mM}$ is defined. No horizontal map is required to be a $k$-morphism.

proof.text:
Write $t_m:Q_1Q_m\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{m+1}$, $d_m:B_1B_m\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{m+1}$, and $c_m:P_1P_m\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{m+1}$ for the inverses of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Put $L=Lp^*$ and let $\theta_r:LQ_r\to B_rL$ be the comparison of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. Apply the first displayed equation of [lem-trf-pullback-coefficient-iterate-coherence] with its $h=p$, $t=h$, and $t_W=\bar g$. Its hypotheses are the equality $p\bar g=hp$ from step 1 and the constant finite coefficient sheaves used here. In that node's notation, $P_r=Q_r$, $Q_r=B_r$, $c_r=\theta_r^{-1}$, $d^X_m=t_m^{-1}$ and $d^W_m=d_m^{-1}$. Inverting its equation therefore gives
$$
\theta_{m+1}\circ L(t_m)=(d_mL)\circ(B_1\theta_m)\circ(\theta_1Q_m).
$$
This is the required equality of the specified derived square comparisons before taking mates.

proof.text:
For $N\in D^b_c(s,A)$, [lem-trf-point-transport-composition] gives, with $V=\operatorname{Fib}_s$,
$$
\iota_N^{(m+1)}=V(t_{m,N})\circ\iota_{Q_mN}^{(1)}\circ\iota_N^{(m)}.
$$
Its finite-field datum, $A=A_{E,n}$ and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ are precisely those fixed in the item, so its maps use the same restriction, colimit insertion, and tensor-unit comparison. The lemma also supplies naturality of $\iota^{(r)}$ for every $r\geq1$ and every derived morphism. In particular it applies to $N=FM$ as used below; the compact-support functor in the item has this bounded constructible target.

proof.text:
Let $u_r:Q_rR\to RB_r$ be the direct-image exchange for the power-$r$ square of $p$, as defined in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (1), or equivalently [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. Apply clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to the degree-$m$ square followed by the degree-one square: all three adjunctions in that clause are $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$, the successive functors on the base are $Q_m,Q_1$, and those on the source are $B_m,B_1$. Their left square comparisons are $Lp^*Q_r\to B_rLp^*$. Step 2 identifies the pasted comparison with the outer one after inserting $t_m,d_m$; [lem-weil-pbc-mate-whisker] moves precisely these changes of the intervening functors through the mate formula (take the source comparison $t_m^{-1}$ and target comparison $d_m$). The mate formula therefore gives the equality, natural in every complex $L$ on $\overline X$,
$$u_{m+1,L}\circ t_{m,RL}=R(d_{m,L})\circ u_{1,B_mL}\circ Q_1(u_{m,L}).$$
This is an identity of the specified mate maps in the ambient pro-etale module derived categories. The geometric hypotheses needed to name them are provided in step 1, and the adjunctions by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. In particular this application does not use an etale-only pasting theorem, or a base-change theorem requiring $k$-linear arrows.

proof.text:
Let $v_r:B_rJ\xrightarrow{\sim}JP_r$ be the open-square exchange for the power-$r$ square of $j$. Apply [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] to the Cartesian squares of step 1; its statement includes naturality and pasting, so with the comparisons of step 2 it gives
$$v_{m+1,M}\circ d_{m,JM}=J(c_{m,M})\circ v_{1,P_mM}\circ B_1(v_{m,M}).$$
These are the very open-square maps used in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (2), on the same $j$ for every power. That definition gives $e_{r,M}=R(v_{r,M})\circ u_{r,JM}$. Use step 4 at $L=JM$, the displayed open pasting equation, and naturality of $u_1$ at $v_{m,M}:B_mJM\to JP_mM$ to calculate
$$\begin{aligned}
e_{m+1,M}t_{m,FM}
 &=R(v_{m+1,M}d_{m,JM})u_{1,B_mJM}Q_1(u_{m,JM})\\
 &=R(J(c_{m,M})v_{1,P_mM})R(B_1(v_{m,M}))u_{1,B_mJM}Q_1(u_{m,JM})\\
 &=F(c_{m,M})R(v_{1,P_mM})u_{1,JP_mM}Q_1(R(v_{m,M}))Q_1(u_{m,JM})\\
 &=F(c_{m,M})e_{1,P_mM}Q_1(e_{m,M}).
\end{aligned}$$
All products here mean composition with the rightmost map first. Thus the identity for $e_r$ is proved from its two factors; it is not assumed as a new compact-support coherence lemma.

proof.text:
Set $N=FM$ and $V=\operatorname{Fib}_s$, so $H=VF$ by [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Naturality of $\iota^{(1)}$ at the derived morphism $e_{m,M}:Q_mFM\to FP_mM$ is exactly clause 2 of [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] at finite coefficients:
$$\iota^{(1)}_{FP_mM}\,V(e_{m,M})=V(Q_1(e_{m,M}))\,\iota^{(1)}_{Q_mFM}.$$
All its objects lie in $D^b_c(s,A)$, the domain already specified for these maps in the item; step 1 also verifies the coefficient input $P_mM$. Substitute this identity, step 5 and step 3 into the definition of the two transports:
$$\begin{aligned}
H(c_{m,M})\tau^{(1)}_{c,P_mM}\tau^{(m)}_{c,M}
 &=V(F(c_{m,M})e_{1,P_mM})\iota^{(1)}_{FP_mM}V(e_{m,M})\iota^{(m)}_{FM}\\
 &=V(F(c_{m,M})e_{1,P_mM}Q_1(e_{m,M}))\iota^{(1)}_{Q_mFM}\iota^{(m)}_{FM}\\
 &=V(e_{m+1,M})V(t_{m,FM})\iota^{(1)}_{Q_mFM}\iota^{(m)}_{FM}\\
 &=V(e_{m+1,M})\iota^{(m+1)}_{FM}=\tau^{(m+1)}_{c,M}.
\end{aligned}$$
This is the asserted identity, with $c_{m,M}$ in the direction specified in the statement. It uses no morphism $P_1M\to M$ and no Weil structure.

proof.text: Finally suppose the fixed compact-support functor is represented by another compactification, written $F_d$, and let $C:F_d\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ be its specified comparison. The prescription in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (2) defines its power-$r$ exchange as $C_{P_rM}^{-1}e_{r,M}Q_r(C_M)$. Naturality of $\iota^{(r)}$, established directly for every $r$ in step 3, then gives $\tau^{(r)}_{d,M}=V(C_{P_rM}^{-1})\tau^{(r)}_{c,M}V(C_M)$. In the right side of the composition identity the two middle comparison factors cancel, and naturality of $C$ at $c_{m,M}$ gives $F_d(c_{m,M})C_{P_1P_mM}^{-1}=C_{P_{m+1}M}^{-1}F(c_{m,M})$. Thus both sides are the corresponding sides for $F$, conjugated by $V(C_M)$ and $V(C_{P_{m+1}M}^{-1})$. Step 6 proves their equality. This only transports a specified map on the same $c_0$; no independence of exchange from a varying compactification is asserted or required.
